claims.text: Refractory HEAs containing tungsten and tantalum have excellent high-temperature strength.
Refractory HEAs containing tungsten and tantalum have strong irradiation resistance.
Tungsten and tantalum generate long-lived radioactive byproducts under fusion-relevant irradiation.
Vanadium, chromium, and molybdenum are lower-activation refractory-element alternatives to tungsten and tantalum.
Reducing or replacing tungsten and tantalum with vanadium, chromium, and molybdenum can maintain overall high-temperature alloy performance.
The adjusted elemental composition can maintain a stable modified solid solution and microstructure.
The maintained solid solution and microstructural stability support the required mechanical strength.
The maintained solid solution and microstructural stability support irradiation resistance.
Replacing high-activation elements with low-activation refractory elements reduces the formation of long-lived radioactive isotopes.
The replacement elemental mixture preserves critical high-temperature strengthening mechanisms by maintaining a stable HEA structure.
Maintaining a stable HEA structure enhances irradiation tolerance.
The tailored HEA will have high-temperature mechanical properties comparable to conventional refractory HEAs.
The tailored HEA will have irradiation resistance comparable to conventional refractory HEAs.
The tailored HEA will generate significantly fewer long-lived radioactive byproducts than conventional refractory HEAs under fusion-reactor conditions.
A compositionally tailored low-activation refractory HEA can serve as a structural material for high-temperature plasma-facing components in fusion reactors.
